scope: Cross-cutting collections gathering events that surface women's political and intellectual agency in subcontinental history. Seeded with the freedom-struggle collection; women rulers, women writers, women in religious reform queued.

collections.title: Women shapers of the freedom struggle
collections.subtitle: From Lakshmibai's 1857 letters to Sarojini Naidu's UP governorship — women whose work shaped the long arc of Indian political agency.
collections.summary: Indian textbook telling tends to flatten the women of the freedom struggle into ornament — Sarojini's poetry, Lakshmibai's bravery, the Bhopal Begums' charity. The events corpus tells a different story: political negotiation at the Round Table, military command at Jhansi, princely administration at Bhopal, anti-patriarchal polemic from Pune. This collection gathers events that surface that work.
collections.framing: The 'long freedom struggle' framing here is deliberate: the collection includes events from 1853 to 1947, a century during which Indian women acted politically across utterly different registers — armed rebellion (Lakshmibai), reform polemic (Pandita Ramabai), princely sovereignty under colonial paramountcy (Sultan Jahan Begum), Congress organising (Sarojini Naidu). Tagged events join automatically; explicit entries below curate the seed. Women rulers (Ahilyabai Holkar, Razia Sultan, the four Bhopal Begums as a series), women in religious reform (Savitribai Phule, the Bengal women of the Brahmo Samaj), Cama and Hazrat Mahal as further freedom-struggle figures, all queued as the corpus grows.
